text:
elaine (marketing): quick ask — can eng-runtime run a targeted probe for sample-selection bias + variance on long-context (>4k) traffic we plan to cite in the launch narrative? mainly worried about percentile stability across quantized vs fp16 variants. need methodology + raw artifacts for claims.

sam (eng-runtime): can do — what's the exact cohort and payload surface? any warmup policy you expect us to replicate (client warmup vs token warmup)? also which quantized variants?

elaine (marketing): cohort = 2K samples drawn from our demo traffic (mix of news summaries, long docs, and code). primary slices: long-context (>4k), medium (1k-4k), short (<1k). payload example below: 

```json
{"prompt": "Summarize the following article in ~3 bullets:", "context": "<~4500 tokens of news article text>", "max_tokens": 256, "temperature": 0.0}
```

elaine (marketing): warmup: try two modes — coldstart (no prefix cache) and representative warmup (single prefix warmup per model like prod). Annotate exact warmup sequence used.

jia (eng-ml): metrics request: p50/p90/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, cost-per-k-token estimate, token-efficiency delta between variants, generation-quality delta (embedding-sim on outputs to reference fp16), and failure/timeout counts. also capture KV-cache hit rates and any divergence in top-k between variants for the same seed.

anil (product): add: please surface any systematic sample bias e.g., certain doc types (code vs news) showing higher variance — we need that callout for messaging. also include reproducibility checklist and minimal runbook so marketing can sanity-check claims.

sam (eng-runtime): noted. we'll run: models = ["redwood-xl-8k-fp16", "redwood-xl-8k-4bit-quant" , "redwood-xl-16k-fp16 (fallback)"]. confirm that quant name is fine? we'll produce per-slice breakdown and trace artifacts.

elaine (marketing): names fine. also need the raw sample IDs + hashed payloads for chain-of-custody. retention: keep raw outputs + traces for 30 days, and export a sanitized CSV for marketing.

sam (eng-runtime): ok — one more: do you want randomized ordering across models or same order for warmup determinism? randomized better for noise estimates, same order better for direct pairwise comparisons.

jia (eng-ml): do both: run randomized repeats (N=5) for variance estimation, then one deterministic paired-run to compute direct deltas. save seeds.

sam (eng-runtime): plan: 1) quick smoke today to validate configs, 2) full sweep (2K samples x 3 slices x 3 models x 6 repeats) — estimate ~36k requests plus warmups. bench-bot will schedule on the dedicated pool.

bench-bot: scheduled job #b-4209876543 on ded-pool-3. ETA 36h for completion, artifacts will land in /artifacts/marketing/4209876543/ (raw-outputs, traces, metrics.csv).

sam (eng-runtime): we'll include a short methodology doc (run config, seed list, warmup commands, exact SDK calls) and a reproducibility script. will tag you when artifacts are ready. ETA ~48h. :+1:

elaine (marketing): perfect — thanks team. please ping if anything blocks; marketing will prep the messaging drafts but will wait on the paired-run numbers for any quantitative claim. :pray:
